name: Traefik
description: Protects against destructive Traefik load balancer operations like stopping \ containers, deleting config, or API deletions.

destructive_patterns.name: traefik-docker-stop
destructive_patterns.description: Stopping the Traefik container halts all traffic routing.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Stopping or killing the Traefik container immediately halts all HTTP/HTTPS \ traffic routing. Every service behind this load balancer becomes unreachable \ until Traefik is restarted.

\ Check container status first: \ docker inspect traefik

\ View logs for issues: \ docker logs traefik

destructive_patterns.name: traefik-docker-rm
destructive_patterns.description: Removing the Traefik container destroys the load balancer.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Removing the Traefik container deletes it entirely, including any runtime \ state, Let's Encrypt certificates stored in the container, and dynamic \ configuration. The container must be recreated from scratch.

\ Stop without removing: \ docker stop traefik

\ Back up certificates first if stored in container volume.

destructive_patterns.name: traefik-compose-down
destructive_patterns.description: docker-compose down on Traefik stops and removes the load balancer.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Running docker-compose down stops and removes Traefik containers, networks, \ and optionally volumes. All traffic routing stops and any non-persisted state \ is lost.

\ To stop without removing: \ docker-compose stop traefik

\ To restart cleanly: \ docker-compose restart traefik

destructive_patterns.name: traefik-kubectl-delete-pod
destructive_patterns.description: Deleting Traefik pods/deployments disrupts traffic routing.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting Traefik pods or deployments removes the load balancer from the \ cluster. If managed by a Deployment, pods will be recreated but with \ downtime. Deleting the Deployment itself stops all traffic routing until \ it is redeployed.

\ Check pod status: \ kubectl get pods -l app=traefik

\ Restart pods without deleting: \ kubectl rollout restart deployment traefik

destructive_patterns.name: traefik-kubectl-delete-ingressroute
destructive_patterns.description: Deleting IngressRoute CRDs removes Traefik routing rules.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
IngressRoute custom resources define how Traefik routes traffic to backend \ services. Deleting them removes those routing rules, making the associated \ services unreachable through the load balancer.

\ List current routes first: \ kubectl get ingressroute

\ Describe a route before deleting: \ kubectl describe ingressroute <name>

destructive_patterns.name: traefik-config-delete
destructive_patterns.description: Removing Traefik config files disrupts load balancer configuration.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting Traefik configuration files removes entrypoint definitions, \ middleware chains, TLS settings, and provider configurations. Traefik \ will fail to start or lose routing rules on the next reload.

\ Back up config first: \ cp traefik.yml traefik.yml.backup

\ Validate config before changes: \ traefik healthcheck

destructive_patterns.name: traefik-api-delete
destructive_patterns.description: DELETE operations against Traefik API can remove routing configuration.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Sending DELETE requests to the Traefik API removes routers, services, or \ middleware from the running configuration. Depending on the provider, these \ changes may be permanent or reverted on restart.

\ Use GET to inspect before deleting: \ curl -X GET http://traefik:8080/api/overview

destructive_patterns.name: traefik-systemctl-stop
destructive_patterns.description: systemctl stop traefik stops the Traefik service.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Stopping the Traefik systemd service shuts down the load balancer process. \ All HTTP/HTTPS traffic routing ceases until the service is restarted.

\ Check status first: \ systemctl status traefik

\ To restart instead: \ systemctl restart traefik

destructive_patterns.name: traefik-service-stop
destructive_patterns.description: service traefik stop stops the Traefik service.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Stopping Traefik via the legacy service command terminates the load balancer. \ All traffic routing stops until the service is manually restarted.

\ Check status first: \ service traefik status

\ Prefer systemctl on systemd systems: \ systemctl status traefik
